PR #54 replaced AlertOverlay's WebSocket with the conviction-alert SSE stream,
justified in its own comment as "the legacy /ws/signals socket had no server
producer". That was true when written. PR #56 (merged) made it false: the
producer now exists at backend/routes/alerts.py, the exact path is registered

normalized to {type: 'signal', signal, ...} which the component's own filter

  * DualGEXBadge.jsx fix
  * useSolsticeSnapshot.js removal -- dead code, defined but never imported

The test is rewritten against the actual WebSocket contract rather than SSE,
and adds the regression case that matters: a frame carrying
{type: 'GAMMA_FLIP'} with no `signal` key must produce NO toast. That is the
pre-#56 shape, and the component filter
(`data.type === 'signal' || data.signal`) must reject it.

Note: the jest run for this file could not be executed in the local harness
(interactive consent block), so the assertions were validated structurally --
each target confirmed present in the component source: the ws/signals URL, the
withWsToken import, the type/signal filter, the `·` label separator, the

test(alerts): fix AlertOverlay test to match real component behavior

   frame is deduplicated. addAlert() has no dedup: it assigns a fresh _id on

   testing behavior the component does not have, so it failed.

2. No unmount between tests. The component registers a visibilitychange

(`data.type === 'signal' || data.signal`), the SIGNAL_LABELS fallback, the
`·` separator, malformed-JSON tolerance (the handler's own try/catch), and
growth to maxVisible. Kept the pre-#56 regression case: a frame shaped
{type: 'GAMMA_FLIP'} with no `signal` key must produce NO toast.

Mutation testing the previous commit found a second genuine hole, and it sits
directly under the R8 durability claim.

The mutation: replace

production actually uses. The acceptance ledger's durability claim rested on an
untested link between the two.

attribute -- the only observable proof that a path was honored is a file on
disk. 9 tests: unset path writes nothing; a configured path creates the file;
data survives close-and-reopen through a separate connection; empty and unusable
paths fall back to memory AND log the fallback; the env is read per call, not
frozen at import.

A silent durability downgrade is the exact failure mode this project keeps
warning about, so the unusable-path branch asserts the WARNING is logged, not
just that the fallback happened.

Side effect caught while writing these: a whitespace-only DUCKDB_PATH is a
RELATIVE path, so the engine created a 1MB file named after the spaces in the
working tree (visible as `?? "backend/   "`). _open_shared_db only falls back on
a FALSY value and "   " is truthy. Fixed in the test with monkeypatch.chdir so

wired, moved real bytes, and rendered nothing -- the exact failure the producer
was added to fix, reproduced one layer up.

Why no test caught it: all six asserted that a frame reached send_json. They
checked the SOCKET, never the CONSUMER. Mutation testing missed it too, because
every mutation still delivered a frame to the socket. Reading the consumer is
what found it.

Fix is in the producer, not the consumer -- AlertOverlay's contract is
reasonable. _signal_frame() normalizes any payload so every emitted frame:
  - sets `type` to the literal "signal" (what the overlay matches on)
  - sets `signal` to the original alert kind (rendered as the badge)
  - preserves the raw kind under `alert_type`
  - stamps `ts` when absent

Two new tests pin the consumer contract by mirroring the overlay's filter.
They were RED before this fix, with the exact discard reason, and are green
after. Three older tests asserted the broken frame shape and now assert the
corrected contract.

Checked the other two push channels for the same defect: /ws/gex/{ticker} has

consumer. The defect was specific to /ws/signals.

fix(ws): serve /ws/signals at the path the client actually opens

The alerts websocket was never reachable. `routes/alerts.py` builds its router
with `APIRouter(prefix="/api/alerts")`, so `@router.websocket("/ws/signals")`
registered at `/api/alerts/ws/signals` -- a path no client opens. AlertOverlay.js
opens `${BACKEND_URL.replace('http','ws')}/ws/signals`, which matched
`server.py`'s greedy `/ws/{topic}` with topic="signals" and landed in
`services/websocket_streamer.py`'s ws_manager instead.

So the producer added in f5c12e18 wrote to `_signal_clients`, a list nothing
read. The channel has been dead on EVERY commit that shipped it, including the
frame-shape normalization in 6aaa7dea. Starlette matches in registration order,
and `/ws/{topic}` is declared at server.py:3857, after the alerts router is
included at 3495.

    ALERTS_DETECTED 1

showed the accept came from websocket_streamer.py:42, not alerts.py.

which never includes `server.py`. The prefix was irrelevant to them and the
route ordering did not exist. This is the same blind spot as the frame-shape
bug -- tests on an isolated router cannot see defects that only exist on the
assembled app.

`app.add_api_websocket_route`, placed before /ws/{topic} so first-match
ordering hands /ws/signals to the alerts handler. Both paths now serve:
/ws/signals (the client) and /api/alerts/ws/signals (direct API use). Route
count is unchanged at 377 apart from the addition.

it is registered BEFORE /ws/{topic}, and that the topic handler does not claim

'/ws/signals is not registered on the app at all'.

    FILTER_PASSES True

A real WebSocket client, the real production trigger, and a frame the overlay
accepts and renders.

fix(ws): stop logging ordinary GEX socket disconnects as fatal errors

server.py's websocket_gex error branch sent its error payload on a socket that
had just failed. The exception that reaches that branch is very often itself a
send failure, or the peer has already gone away, so the socket is in ERROR
state and `await websocket.send_json(...)` raises:

    LocalProtocolError: Can't send data when our state is ERROR

That escaped to the outer `except Exception` and was logged at ERROR level:

    WebSocket fatal error for SPY: received 1001 (going away); then sent 1001

So every routine browser disconnect -- a page reload, a tab close, the 5-second
heartbeat reconnect -- was reported as a fatal websocket failure. The live
backend has been emitting these continuously, which is noise that trains you to
ignore ERROR-level logs.

Fix: reporting is best-effort. The send is wrapped, and a failure to deliver
means the socket is gone, so the loop exits instead of retrying a dead peer. The
real underlying error is still logged as a warning with its consecutive count,
so no diagnostic is lost.

production symptom first:

All three were red before the fix. Note how they assert: the outer handler
swallows the escaped exception, so `pytest.raises` PASSES against the buggy
code. The tests assert on the LOG -- no "fatal error" record must appear, and
the underlying warning must still be there. A structural test pins the `try:`
so the guard cannot be quietly removed by a refactor of the surrounding loop.

rows.body:
Audit + workflow-completion pass over `main` (71f83625). 20 commits, in an isolated worktree so it never touched the other agent's tree.

**Standing rule: no finding is actioned until it is reproduced on the current tree.** Both supplied audits were written against *other* commits and contained many claims that were already fixed or never true. Two of my own fixes in this branch were also caught being wrong by the guards I added. Evidence table: [`docs/audit/CLAIMS-VERIFIED.md`](docs/audit/CLAIMS-VERIFIED.md).

## The product bugs (what actually mattered)

**The Charm tab never had data.** `SkylitHeatmapGrid` maps Charm → `grid.charm_grid`, but only the local Black-Scholes path emitted it. The *vendor-greek* path — what actually serves the app — returned no `charm_grid`, so selecting Charm always rendered "surface unavailable in this snapshot" on a healthy payload. Added `compute_charm_grid_local` mirroring the VEX surface, wired into `server.py` with its own status. Missing coverage reports `PARTIAL_CHARM_COVERAGE`; an absent Greek is never zero-filled.

**The WallInspector "VEX gross / net" row was permanently "—".** It read `grids.grid.vex_grid`, but `metrics.grids` is a *map of named overlays* (`{raw, delta, activity, vendor}`), so `grids.grid` was always undefined. VEX lives on the payload's own `grid.vex_grid`. The existing test fixture had encoded the *same mistake*, which is why it passed while broken — fixture corrected.

**Triad had three permanently-blank columns and a wrong-expiry bug.** IV, Delta and per-row expiry don't exist on the `/api/data` heatmap payload (its strike rows carry exactly 27 aggregate keys — verified by calling the route). So the trade panel opened with no IV/delta, and `row.expiry || expiries[0]` requested the *wrong* contract expiry. Real IV/delta/expiry live on `/api/chain/{ticker}`. Repointed at fields that exist, and fixed a stale `useCallback` dep this exposed.

**`CLAUDE.md` claimed `OrderRouter` "has no callers"** — so that its default-deny MARKET gate "protects nothing". False: `discord_bot.py` builds it, making it the only paper-order path. A doc saying a live gate protects nothing is exactly what gets someone to weaken it.

**Schwab removed entirely** (retired 2026-09-03, deleted 2026-09-27): two services, six test modules, two Grafana panels that charted dead metrics, and a runbook telling operators to restart a streamer that no longer exists. `mock_schwab_feed` → `mock_synthetic_feed` (it was never a broker connection — a GBM generator behind a dev flag). Guards now fail if it returns.

## CI/infra that never ran

- The **silent-except gate had never once executed** — `working-directory: backend` with the script at repo root, exit 2 on every push.
- **Observability stack mounted the wrong directory** (6 binds → the repo's *parent*), so Prometheus and Grafana came up with no config and no dashboards, reporting healthy.
- Grafana fought the dev frontend for `:3000`; prod Prometheus had no `extra_hosts` and was never scraping.
- API reference had an **empty Path cell in all 159 rows**; spec held 156 paths against 369 real routes.
- `CLAUDE.md` told you to run a nonexistent Windows venv and **forbade the one that works**.
- The secret-scan gate was scanning a **different repository**.

## Gates

| | |
|---|---|
| Backend | **13 failed / 5429 passed** — failure list **byte-identical** to the pre-change baseline |
| Frontend | **72/72 suites, 619/619 tests**; production build compiles |
| Lint | ruff clean across the backend |

Every new test was verified to **fail against the original broken code** before being trusted. Two intermediate regressions were caught by existing tests during this work, which is the point of having them.

## Two things I did not do

- **Secret rotation** for anything ever committed (`db-PBRQ…` in git history). Rotate at the provider, *then* purge. History rewrites need explicit authorization.
- **Did not delete the unverified dead-code list.** Spot-checks found it wrong (13 dead frontend modules, not 17; a "shadowed route" that was never shadowed).

## The 13 red tests

Pre-existing on `main` since 2026-09-04. **Hermes fixed them on `feat/node-confluence-overlay` (PR #56, `f0fe42d4`) but that branch is not merged**, so they are not in `main`. This branch does not touch any of those files.

No merge without authorization.

fix(ci+docs): repair the lint gate that never ran, and the API docs nobody could use

Audit sweep of main (71f83625). Five real defects, each reproduced before
and after the fix. No product code paths changed.

1. THE SILENT-EXCEPT GATE NEVER RAN.
   lint.yml ran `python3 qc/audit/check_silent_excepts.py` with
   working-directory: backend, but the script lives at repo-root qc/audit/.
   Every push and PR died with "can't open file .../backend/qc/audit/..."
   and exit 2. Reproduced both ways: from backend/ -> exit 2; from the repo
   root -> "OK, 286 files scanned", exit 0. The step now runs at the root,
   where it actually works.

2. lint.yml PINNED python 3.11; THE SHIPPED RUNTIME IS 3.12.
   Dockerfile.backend:1, deploy.yml:52 and ci.yml:48 all say 3.12, and
   pyproject.toml:3-12 records that the 3.11 comment was already corrected.
   lint.yml was the last file still asserting the old runtime.

3. THE "KNOWN RED" BLOCK DOCUMENTED A BUG FIXED FIVE COMMITS AGO.
   It claimed routes/quant.py:187 used a PEP 701 f-string and that the gate
   would fail closed on 3.11. Commit d29ae3fa ("repair Python 3.11
   SyntaxError") already fixed it; quant.py:187 is now a plain dict key, and
   an ast.parse(feature_version=(3,11)) sweep finds ZERO backend files that
   fail 3.11 grammar. The warning was steering people toward a dead end.

4. THE API REFERENCE WAS UNUSABLE AND THE SPEC WAS 57% WRONG.
   docs/api/README.md listed all 159 endpoints with an EMPTY Path column --
   a reference you cannot call anything with. docs/api/openapi.json held
   156 paths against 369 real routes, and nothing anywhere regenerated
   either. qc/audit/generate_api_docs.py now builds both from the live
   FastAPI app (357 paths / 367 operations), and lint.yml gates on
   `--check` so a route added without regenerating fails the build.

5. THE DOCKERFILE SAID SOMETHING FALSE ABOUT TORCH.
   It claimed torch was "ONLY used by backend/tests/* (never imported by
   server.py or any service at runtime)". Five runtime modules import it:
   services/anomaly_detector.py, services/ml_ensemble.py, routes/anomaly.py,
   routes/llm.py, services/memory/chart_embeddings.py. All five guard the
   import (module-scope try/except ImportError, or lazy inside functions), so
   production degrades instead of crashing -- the exclusion is still
   correct, the justification was not. That false claim is exactly what
   would let someone "fix" a guarded import by deleting the guard.

New tests (9, all green): test_api_docs_freshness.py pins the generated-doc
invariants, including that spec and README path sets are equal;
test_docker_torch_boundary.py fails if any module-scope torch import
appears, and fails if the false claim is reintroduced. Both were verified
against the ORIGINAL broken files and do fail there.

Gates: ruff clean across the backend; 9/9 new tests pass. Full baseline is
13 failed / 5392 passed -- all 13 reproduced identically on a pristine
worktree of main and in the untouched shared tree, so no new debt. 3 of the
13 (test_verify_runner) are environmental: they need a local backend/.venv
that neither a fresh worktree nor a worktree-built CI runner has.

fix(qc): make the API-docs gate deterministic (it was a 1-in-3 coin toss)

Wiring --check into CI exposed a nondeterminism bug in the generator added in
the previous commit. Identical source, different output, roughly 1 run in 3.

Cause: server.py registers the root health probe as both @app.get("/") and
@app.head("/"). FastAPI derives operationId from name+path+method; when two
routes collide it warns "Duplicate Operation ID" and the winner is decided by
set iteration order, which varies per interpreter run. So the committed
openapi.json flipped between "root_head__head" and "root_head__get" on
identical input, and the new CI gate would have failed roughly a third of
builds for no reason.

Fix: assign every operation a stable id computed from method+path instead of
FastAPI's colliding generated one. Ids remain unique because the method is
part of the key, and they no longer depend on route registration order.

Verified: 6/6 consecutive --check runs now pass (previously flaky at the same
rate), and two consecutive generations are byte-identical.

Two new tests pin it: test_operation_ids_are_unique_and_stable (fails against
the previous spec, which carried the collision) and
test_generation_is_reproducible. 38 tests green across the three new files;
ruff clean.

fix: three real defects (dead OI parser, blank Net Γ row, dead signal channel)

An audit v2 was supplied describing this repo at 7fed6012. Before acting on
it I re-verified every claim against main (71f83625). MOST of its headline
findings were already fixed here and it is wrong about them — see the PR
body. These three survived verification and are fixed now.

1. parse_osi could never succeed (silent, live-path).
   OSI_RE captures SIX groups (underlying, YY, MM, DD, C/P, strike) but the
   function unpacked FOUR names, so every call raised
   `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 4, got 6)`.
   fetch_oi_for_ticker is called from server.py:709 and :2465, so the
   Databento OI overlay was wired, always failed, and the circuit breaker
   kept it off. Now unpacked by position and documented.

2. The Net Γ row in MultiTimeframeGEXPanel was permanently blank.
   The panel read `v.net_gamma`; the endpoint it calls
   (GET /gex-timeframes/{ticker} -> services/gex_history.py:341) returns
   `net_gex`. No endpoint emits `net_gamma`, so the cell could only ever
   render "—". Fixed with the correct key plus a `??` alias.

3. /ws/signals had clients but no producer.
   `_signal_clients` was appended to on connect and never read, so
   AlertOverlay connected cleanly, sat silent forever, and showed no alerts
   — a dead channel that looked healthy because nothing crashed. Added
   `broadcast_signal()`, which stamps type/ts for the frontend's onmessage
   filter and evicts dead clients so one wedged socket cannot silence the
   fanout for everyone.

4. The secret-scan gate was scanning a different repository.
   tests/chaos/test_secret_scan.py hardcoded
   `/Users/nav/Documents/GitHub/floww` — a stale clone, not this repo — for
   both the import path and the tree scan. The gate therefore passed while
   scanning the wrong tree and could never have caught a credential pasted
   here, and on CI that path does not exist at all. Now derived from
   __file__, and widened to cover .github and docs. With the fix it scans
   this repo and reports ZERO real secrets — so the audit's "5 plaintext
   credentials in MASTER_PLAN.md" is stale; those were already cleaned.
   test_gate_scans_the_repo_it_ships_in guards against the regression
   without hardcoding a directory name, so worktrees still pass.

Gates: 30 new/existing tests green; 601 passed on the alert+databento+osi
selection; ruff clean. New tests were each verified to FAIL against the
original broken code (parse_osi: 6 of 8 failed before the fix).

docs: CLAUDE.md pointed at a venv that does not exist and forbade the one that works

The most actively harmful stale claim in the repo. CLAUDE.md told every
reader (and every agent) to run:

    backend/.venv313/Scripts/python.exe

That path is wrong three ways: there is no `.venv313` directory, it is a
Windows `Scripts/*.exe` form in a POSIX repo, and the same section explicitly
said "never backend/.venv" — which is the venv that actually has pytest and
ruff. Following the doc sent you to a missing binary, or told you to avoid
the only working interpreter. 11 command lines across the file were affected,
plus a Dev Environment section describing a different, retired Windows 11 box
(3.13.15 / Node 24 / cargo 1.94 / PowerShell) as "this machine".

Corrected against the real sources of truth:
  * Python 3.12   <- Dockerfile.backend:1, ci.yml, deploy.yml
  * Node 20       <- Dockerfile.frontend, ci.yml, deploy.yml
  * React 19      <- frontend/package.json (was claimed as 18)
  * ruff target-version = "py311", not "py313" — and it must track
    requires-python, since a target above the runtime makes ruff propose
    syntax the shipped interpreter cannot parse.

README.md also claimed Python 3.11 in two places.

New tests/test_version_doc_consistency.py pins all of it against the real
files rather than hardcoded values: shipped Python must match across
Dockerfile/ci.yml/pyproject, ruff target must not exceed the requires-python
floor, CLAUDE.md may not contain a runnable command referencing the Windows
venv, and neither doc may state a React major the app does not use. The
venv test inspects command lines only, so the prose explaining the old
mistake does not trip it — and it asserts no fixed directory name, so
worktrees and CI checkouts pass.

Verified against the original docs: 3 of the 5 fail there, all 5 pass now.
ruff clean; 35 tests green across all files added in this series.

Note: parsing this surfaced that ruff writes target-version as "py311" with no

fix(ml): refuse to predict on feature-schema drift instead of zero-filling it

POST /predict/{ticker} built its inference vector with:

    X = np.array([[features.get(name, 0.0) for name in model_feature_names]])

Any feature the serve path did not produce became 0.0. That is a
perfectly ordinary value for most of these features — net GEX, ratios,
z-scores — so a model trained on 44 features and served with 14 returned a
confident UP/HOLD/DOWN built partly from fabricated zeros. Nothing was logged
and no error was raised, so a caller could not distinguish a real prediction
from a broken one. On a scoring surface that feeds the conviction rank and
the agent copilot, silent wrong confidence is worse than an outage.

Now a missing feature returns 409 `feature_schema_mismatch` naming the
offenders and the expected count, and non-finite inputs return 409
`non_finite_features`. Both log at ERROR first. The vector is now built with
strict indexing, so a typo in a feature name raises rather than defaulting.

The NaN/inf guard is deliberately separate: the old zero-fill produced
*finite* values, so a finiteness check alone would never have caught this.

New tests/test_ml_schema_guard.py (6) covers the detection, documents what
the old expression produced, covers the non-finite path and the all-present
path, and asserts via tokenize (CODE tokens only, not comments — the
explanatory comment quotes the old line on purpose) that the zero-fill
lookup cannot silently return. 9 passed on the ml selection; ruff clean.

rows.title: docs(audit): record unverified artifacts the CI truth audit does not surface
rows.body:
## What

`qc/audit/truth_audit.sh` runs as step 4 of every CI `backend-tests` job and is
the repo's only automated overfit check. Its model rules (9-12) only **block**
when the commit subject claims ML work; on anything else they print `WARN`.
That scoping is deliberate — the script's comments say enforcing
unconditionally "would block unrelated work on pre-existing model debt — the
fastest way to get a gate switched off."

So normal commits report `24 passed, 0 failed` while the debt is unread.

## The finding

Reproduced on `origin/main` with an empty commit that trips the trigger
(`git commit --allow-empty -m 'chore: quarantine degenerate models'`):

**6 violations across 24 audited models.** All live under `backend/models/`,
none quarantined, all trained 2026-05-24.

| Model | Finding |
|---|---|
| `SPY_rf_20260524_020801` | **`avg_test_sharpe` 8.0202** (threshold 5), accuracy 0.82 |
| `SPY_rf_20260524_020801` | ratio **0.28125** — 45 features / 160 samples |
| `IWM_rf_20260524_022147` | ratio 0.275 — 44 / 160 |
| `TLT_rf_20260524_022154` | ratio 0.275 — 44 / 160 |
| `QQQ_rf_20260524_022055` | ratio 0.275 — 44 / 160 |
| `QQQ_rf_20260524_022118` | ratio 0.275 — 44 / 160 |

Every figure was re-read from the JSON directly, not taken from the audit's own
output — a gate reporting its own findings is not independent verification.

## What this is not

A measurement, not a verdict. Nothing is retrained or quarantined here. Four
tickers failing the identical ratio at the identical sample count points at one
shared training configuration, not four independent problems, and whether 44
features on 160 samples is acceptable is a modeling decision.

The Sharpe 8.02 is the one to look at first: above 5 on *daily direction* is
the exact signature Rule 9 exists to catch.

**This is not evidence of predictive skill.** An overfit artifact is evidence
about the fitting procedure, not about the market. Docs only.

## The gap

`qc/audit/truth_audit.sh` runs as step 4 of every CI `backend-tests` job and is
the repo's only automated overfit check. Its discovery:

    find models backend/models -maxdepth 2 -type f \
        \( -name '*_meta_*.json' -o -name '*_meta.json' -o -name 'meta_*.json' \)

matches three patterns and finds **8** descriptors. This repo also uses
`*_manifest.json` — matched by none of them. Adding it finds **84**.

So 76 descriptors were invisible to rules 9-12, including all 11 live
root-tree manifests.

## What it was hiding

`models/SPY_gbm_production_manifest.json`:

    n_features 53, n_samples 167  ->  ratio 0.3174  (threshold 0.2)  VIOLATION

This is the one that matters. It is production-named, and it lives in the
directory the live loader actually reads — `ml_price_prediction.py:210-218`
resolves repo-root `models/`. Its own `gate_results` record only
`class_balance`, `feature_variance`, `prediction_distribution`: no Sharpe
ceiling, no sample floor, no ratio. The overfit guards were never run against it.

It also violates the ratio rule more severely than any of the six descriptors
the gate *did* inspect (0.3174 vs 0.28125) — those six are in
`backend/models/`, which no code path globs.

## Proof

Measured in a throwaway worktree, before and after:

    before:  grep -c SPY_gbm_production_manifest  ->  0        (blind to it)
    after:   ratio 0.31736526946107785 > 0.2 (53 features / 167 samples)  FAIL

## Enforcement scoping is unchanged

The existing WARN/FAIL split still holds, and is what makes this safe:

| Commit subject | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| does not claim ML work | 24 passed, 0 failed | **226 passed, 0 failed** (new findings print WARN) |
| claims ML/model work | 6 findings, FAIL | **7 findings, FAIL** |

Unrelated work is not blocked; a commit that actually touches these artifacts
now fails on a violation it previously could not see.

No change was needed to the metric extractor — `n_samples` and `n_features` are
top-level in this schema and `first()` already handles them without
`fold_details`. **Absent stays `NA`:** `SPY_gbm_production` records no sharpe,
and the gate correctly prints `SKIP / NOT verified` rather than scoring it.

## Scope

No model is retrained, quarantined, or deleted. This changes what the gate can
see, nothing about the models themselves. Whether 53 features on 167 samples is
acceptable remains a separate judgment call, recorded in #60.

rows.body:
## Why

`qc/audit/truth_audit.sh` runs as step 4 of every CI `backend-tests` job and is
the repo's only automated overfit check. Its silent-except sibling has 27
tests. This one had **none** — which is how it went on inspecting 8 of 84 model
descriptors while reporting `PASS`, until #61 widened the `find`.

A gate with no test of its own is one rename away from silently covering less,
and it will not tell you.

## What is covered

21 tests, all over `tmp_path` fixtures. None read the live model tree, so only
changing the gate's own behaviour can break them.

- **Discovery** — each of the four filename conventions must still match
  something, and five real descriptors must stay reachable. This is the direct
  guard on the #61 regression.
- **The four metric verdicts** — ratio ceiling, Sharpe ceiling, healthy pass,
  and `absent` → `SKIP`.
- **The WARN/FAIL split** — a ratio violation must WARN and exit 0 on a docs
  commit; a clean docs commit must pass. A gate that blocks unrelated work gets
  switched off, which is worse than one that under-reports.
- **Subject-line scoping** — `model` in a commit *body* must not trip the ML
  rules.

## Two of my own assertions were wrong

Both caught by running the gate rather than reasoning about it:

1. A fixture with `sharpe` under `metrics.sharpe` scored `SKIP`. The extractor
   reads Sharpe from the document root only, and the real
   `SPY_gbm_production_manifest.json` records no Sharpe anywhere — its `metrics`
   block holds train/test accuracy, precision, recall, f1, `train_samples`. My
   fixture had invented a schema the gate does not read; `SKIP` was correct.
2. A docs commit over an empty model tree "should" pass. It must **not**: the
   gate fails when it inspects zero descriptors, which is right — a `find`
   matching nothing is exactly the shape #61 had.

## Mutation-verified

Reverting the #61 `find` pattern in a scratch worktree turns **8 of these red**,
including `test_manifest_fixtures_are_inspected`, the direct guard on the
discovery regression.

    with fix:     21 passed
    fix reverted:  8 failed, 13 passed

Test-only. No gate or model behaviour changed.

fix(qc): make the truth-audit fixture independent of ambient git config

The first CI run of this suite went red: 7 of 21 tests failed with
git commit exiting 128 inside the tmp_path fixture. Every one of them passed
locally, which is the part worth writing down.

The fixture built a real git repo because truth_audit.sh derives REPO_ROOT
from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and reads the commit subject. That made it
depend on git settings the test does not own.

Fixed by passing them per-invocation instead of inheriting them:

  -c user.name / user.email   identity is not guaranteed on a runner
  -c commit.gpgsign=false     a configured signing key would fail the commit
  -c safe.directory=*         git >= 2.35 refuses a directory owned by another
                              user with exit 128, and tmp_path ownership is
                              not guaranteed to match the runner

The commit call now captures stderr and asserts on it, so a future failure
names the setting instead of reporting a bare exit 128.

I could not reproduce the original failure locally: stripping identity via
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, HOME and env -i all left the suite green, and a hand-built
fixture repo committed fine. So the trigger is environmental and I have not
proven which setting it was. The change makes the fixture hermetic against all
three candidates rather than claiming to have identified the culprit.

Re-verified: 21 pass with the #61 fix, 8 fail with it reverted in a scratch
worktree. Test-only.

rows.title: fix(agent,compose,api): unblock CI on three independent failures
rows.body:
Fixes two independent CI failures, both reproduced rather than inferred.

## 1. `fix(agent)` — unjustified silent except

```
backend/services/agent/model.py:214: pass    [unjustified]
1 unjustified silent handler site(s) across 326 scanned file(s).
```

A 6-line justification comment. No behaviour change — the production diff is
6 insertions, 0 deletions.

Before writing the comment I checked whether the swallow was actually
*correct*, because a justification that misstates the reason is worse than
none. It is correct, and specifically so:

- a failed settlement must not fail the request;
- `accounted` stays `False`, so the result reports `accounting="reserved"` and
  `actual_cost=None` rather than claiming the generation was billed;
- `reconcile()` looks the generation up by id via `GET /generation`, which
  never repeats the paid request.

The two neighbouring handlers already use `contextlib.suppress`, which reads as
self-documenting. This one used `try/except: pass`, so the intent was invisible.

Nothing pinned the behaviour — the swallow could have become "report settled
anyway" and no test would have noticed. `tests/agent/test_settlement_failure_path.py`
covers both halves of the split.

**Mutation-verified:** reverting the swallow to claim success
(`accounted = True` in the handler) fails
`test_failed_settlement_reports_reserved_and_never_claims_billed`. That is the
exact regression that would tell the ledger a generation was billed when the
reservation was never consumed.

## 2. `docs(api)` — 13 undocumented routes

The "API docs match the app" step also failed. It is **not** caused by the
settlement change: it reproduces on clean `origin/main`, so it is a
pre-existing failure the earlier integration left behind.

13 routes are live in the app but missing from the committed snapshot
(357 → 370 paths), including several this repo's own audit work added or
verified live earlier — `node-confluence` and the `universe` scan/leaderboard
routes:

```
/api/agent/{history,models,session,session/logout,session/recover,session/rotate}
/api/flowseeker/{market-session,universe/leaderboard,universe/scan}
/api/heatseeker/{node-confluence,price-history/{ticker}}
/api/market/{catalog,provider-updates}
```

Checked rather than assumed:

- `generate_api_docs.py --check` now exits 0: `API docs up to date (370 paths)`
- **0 new order-placement routes.** The `/api/alpaca/order*` paths present in
  the snapshot pre-date this change and were already documented, so
  regenerating does not widen the data router's surface.
- **0 paths removed.** Every previously documented route survives.

## Evidence

- `tests/agent/`: 410 passed (408 before, 2 added)
- `tests/test_compose_consistency.py`: 31 passed
- `ruff`: clean
- `check_silent_excepts.py`: OK, 326 files
- `truth_audit.sh`: 228 passed, 0 failed

### A local failure that is not a code defect

`test_schwab_is_fully_removed_from_the_tree` failed locally with
`retired Schwab artifacts are back: ['backend/tests/schwab']`. That directory
held only gitignored `__pycache__/*.pyc` leftovers from an earlier session and
zero tracked files, so removing it cleared the local run.

Verified it does not affect CI: on a pristine checkout of this branch the test
fails for an unrelated reason (`bind-mount sources that do not exist:
frontend/build`), and passes 31/31 once `frontend/build` exists — which CI's
frontend job produces before the backend job runs.

## Note

The local venv needed `mongomock-motor` and `hypothesis` installed. Both are
already declared (`requirements.txt:92`, `requirements-test.txt`); they were
missing locally only.

The only other dirty file in the tree is `kanban/BOTTLENECK_ALERTS.md`, which
belongs to another agent and is deliberately not staged here.

test(compose): exempt gitignored build outputs from the bind-mount existence check

CI backend-tests failed on main with 6357 passed / 1 failed:

  test_every_bind_mount_source_exists[docker-compose.prod.yml]
  bind-mount sources that do not exist: ['docker-compose.prod.yml:caddy -> ./frontend/build']

The mount is correct. `frontend/build` is gitignored (frontend/.gitignore:12) and
is produced by the frontend job, which runs on a separate runner with its own
filesystem. It is absent in a fresh checkout by design, so the check was
asserting against an artifact that legitimately does not exist yet.

Note a `needs:` edge would NOT fix this. Ordering backend-tests after
frontend-build still leaves frontend/build absent, because separate jobs do not
share a workspace. Only an uploaded artifact or a shared workspace would, and
neither is warranted for a path the build recreates on every deploy.

So the fix belongs in the test. The exemption uses git's own ignore rules via
`git check-ignore` rather than a hardcoded list of directory names, so a new
build output is exempt automatically while a misspelled mount is still caught.

Mutation-verified both directions:
  - pristine checkout with no frontend/build -> 31 passed
  - docker-compose.prod.yml mount mutated to ./frontend/buidl -> FAILS with
    'bind-mount sources that do not exist: ... ./frontend/buidl'

The guard is weakened only for gitignored paths; a typo is not ignored, so the
regression this test was written for still fails it.

The local run also tripped on a stale backend/tests/schwab/__pycache__
directory left by an earlier session. That was gitignored bytecode with zero
tracked files, not a code defect, and does not occur in CI.

rows.title: docs: restore the CLAUDE.md venv fix that a side-branch recovery reverted
rows.body:
`test_version_doc_consistency::test_claude_md_does_not_point_at_a_nonexistent_windows_venv`
fails on main. **The test is correct — the doc had regressed.**

## What happened

`abb8c488` ("CLAUDE.md pointed at a venv that does not exist and forbade the one
that works") fixed this deliberately and added the test. Its message states
plainly that *there is no `.venv313` directory* and that the Windows
`Scripts/*.exe` form is wrong for a POSIX repo.

Then `a590d0e3` — "Recover useful side-branch work with verified reconciliation
evidence" — reintroduced all 12 `.venv313` lines. `abb8c488` is an **ancestor** of
`a590d0e3`, so the side-branch recovery overwrote a fix that was already merged.

## The misdiagnosis I nearly shipped

This looked identical to the compose bind-mount bug fixed in #63 — an assertion
about a path that only exists on one machine. I wrote a `sys.platform == "win32"`
guard to scope the check to Windows, and it passed locally.

Then I read the original commit message. The author considered the path wrong on
**every** platform, not just non-Windows. So the guard would have silenced a
correct check to make a red test go green — the wrong fix for a real doc bug.
That patch is reverted and is **not** in this commit.

## What changed, each verified against this checkout

- **8 runnable commands** pointed at `.venv313/Scripts/python.exe` now use
  `cd backend && .venv/bin/python`. Confirmed working: `--collect-only`
  collects 6410 tests; `uvicorn` imports.
- **The ruff line claimed the venv provides ruff. It does not** —
  `python -m ruff` returns `No module named ruff`. Ruff is a standalone binary
  at `/opt/homebrew/bin/ruff` (0.15.22). The doc now says that.
- **The Dev Environment claimed the venv is Python 3.12. It is 3.14.6** — newer
  than the 3.12 ship pin, so it can accept syntax the image would not. The doc
  now warns about that and points at `ruff` `target-version` and
  `requires-python` as the authority.
- **The "Windows environments" block claimed `backend/.venv/bin/python` does not
  exist and told readers to avoid it.** That is the exact inverse of reality
  and was the most harmful line in the file. Replaced with verified local facts.

The one surviving `.venv313` mention is prose stating the directory is *absent*,
which the test permits by design — its docstring says it checks command lines
only, so prose explaining the old path was wrong does not trip the gate.

## Evidence

- `test_version_doc_consistency.py`: 5 passed
- 90 passed across version-doc + compose + truth-audit + silent-except suites
- `truth_audit.sh`: passed, 0 failed

Docs only — 1 file, no code, no test, no config.

rows.title: chore(gitignore): cover the SQLite runtime stores the duckdb rules missed
rows.body:
Running the backend left three untracked files in `backend/data/`:

```
backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3
backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3-wal
backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3-shm
```

A dirty tree from merely starting the server is how runtime state ends up
committed by accident, and it masks real changes in `git status`.

## The existing rules were half-dead

`.gitignore` had `data/*.duckdb` and `data/*.duckdb.wal`. A pattern containing a
slash is **anchored to the directory holding the .gitignore**, so `data/*.duckdb`
only ever matched the **repo-root** `data/`. It never reached `backend/data/` at
all — and the sqlite store that appeared there was covered by no rule whatsoever.

## Verified with `git check-ignore` on each real path

| path | after |
|---|---|
| `data/journal.duckdb` | IGNORED |
| `data/journal.duckdb.wal` | IGNORED |
| `backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3` | IGNORED |
| `backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3-wal` | IGNORED |
| `backend/data/scan_observations.sqlite3-shm` | IGNORED |

## Two stores deliberately NOT matched

```
data/research_kg.duckdb        (23 MB, tracked)
backend/data/gflows.duckdb     (1 MB, tracked)
```

Both are **committed** to the repo, and ignoring a tracked file does nothing
anyway. Whether they belong in git is a separate question this PR does not
touch — adding patterns for them would be misleading, since it would suggest
they are ignored when they are in fact tracked.

The repo-root patterns are kept alongside the new `backend/` ones because **both**
`data/` directories are real and both hold runtime state. My first pass concluded
the root `data/` did not exist and removed the old rules; a directory listing
showed otherwise, so the old rules are preserved and extended.

1 file, `.gitignore` only.

rows.title: fix(requirements,test): make @pytest.mark.flaky functional and seed the test that flaked
rows.body:
Two related defects, found by an actual failure rather than by inspection.

## 1. `@pytest.mark.flaky` was inert on 8 tests

`backend/pytest.ini` registers a `flaky` marker and 8 tests use it, but
`pytest-rerunfailures` was in no requirements file. Pytest accepts unknown
markers silently, so it looked active and was not — a flaky test was reported as
a plain failure with no retry, **in CI as well as locally**. CI installs
`-r requirements.txt`, so the runner was affected too.

Proven, not inferred — a marker with `reruns=3` that needed 3 attempts:

```
ATTEMPTS = 1        # with the plugin installed this prints 3
```

## 2. The test that actually flaked

`test_overfit_small_dataset` trains a 100-step Adam run and asserts
`final_loss < 0.01`. Neither the input draw (`torch.randn`) nor the model init
was seeded. Measured over 120 unseeded runs of the same loop:

```
min=0.00046  max=0.02332  mean=0.00312
over the 0.01 threshold: 1 of 120   (0.83%)
```

That matches the one real failure observed in a full local run
(`1 failed, 6379 passed`) with nothing else in flight.

Seeded with `torch.manual_seed(0)`:

- same seed twice → byte-identical loss `0.00315112`
- seed `7` → `0.0032903`, so the seed is load-bearing, not a no-op
- 8 consecutive isolated runs pass; 17/17 in the file

**This is the underlying fix.** `reruns=2` only converted a ~1%-periodic failure
into a ~0.5% one, and until the plugin is installed the marker does nothing at
all. Seeding removes the variance instead of retrying around it.

## Not verified locally

`pip install pytest-rerunfailures` was blocked awaiting consent, so the local
venv still lacks the plugin. The requirements change is what CI reads.

2 files: `backend/requirements.txt` (+5), `backend/tests/services/test_anomaly_training.py` (+6).

rows.body:
Found by mutation while auditing `91c7c032`, not by reading the test file.

## The gap

`services/public_session_close.py` accepts a completed-session bar only if

```python
0 < bar['l'] <= min(bar['o'], bar['c']) <= max(bar['o'], bar['c']) <= bar['h']
and bar['v'] >= 0
```

`test_bad_close_fails_closed` varies **only the close**, which the ordering
constraint already rejects. The positivity and volume halves were unpinned.

Weakening `0 < bar['l']` to `-1e18 < bar['l']` left all 26 tests green:

```
# before
MUTATED: EXIT=0   26 passed
```

The new `test_implausible_bar_fields_fail_closed` — negative low, zero low,
negative volume, infinite high, NaN low — each fails for exactly one reason, and
the same mutation is now caught:

```
# after
MUTATED: EXIT=1   2 failed, 29 passed
restored: 31 passed, production file back to no diff
```

A negative low would be accepted as a real session close and flow into the spot
observation, so this is a data-integrity guard, not a formatting one.

## A correction worth keeping

The first version of this test used the **normalized short keys** (`l`, `v`) and
all 5 cases failed against *correct* production code:

```
assert 771.35 is None
```

`_extract_bars` maps the vendor's `open/high/low/close/volume` onto short keys,
so the fixture must set the long names. A test failing against correct code is a
broken test, not a discovered bug — establish which before touching production.

Production code is unchanged in this PR: `git diff --quiet
services/public_session_close.py` is clean, and ruff passes.

rows.title: fix: fail closed and correct time/DST handling across 9 sites
rows.body:
## What

Stops `conviction_rank` from scoring **absent** evidence as **neutral**
confidence, and stops direction from leaking into quality.

## Why this is not the mechanism the audit described

The packet said the flow is "fuses a score once, then passes the fused score as
the flow input into rank_many, which fuses it again. Reproduced 73 -> 67.05."

The code does not do that. `flowseeker.py:2684` passes the fused blob as the
`conviction` **payload field**; it never passes a fused score as `flow`. The
real defects were three different things, all reproduced before fixing.

## The three defects

**1. Missing normalized to 0.5, not 0.0.** `_norm_conf` and `_norm_ml` returned
`0.5` for absent input while `_norm_flow` and `_norm_opp` returned `0.0`. So a
setup with no evidence at all scored:

```
ALL-MISSING conviction: 17.5 tier: LOW
components: {'flow': 0.0, 'opportunity': 0.0, 'confluence': 0.5, 'ml': 0.5}
statuses:   all four 'missing'
```

That 17.5 is entirely `0.2*0.5 + 0.15*0.5` from the two scorers holding no
data. The module's own `*_status` fields said "missing" while the component
said 0.5 — the values contradicted each other. It also outranked real-but-weak
evidence.

**2. Direction leaked into quality.** `_norm_ml` mapped DOWN→0.0 and UP→1.0,
then applied confidence around 0.5, so BULLISH at 0.8 confidence became 0.95
and the identical BEARISH mirror became 0.05. `_norm_conf` had the same shape:
`(v+100)/200` made a signed 0 read as 0.5. The docstring says the module
"never invents direction"; the arithmetic did. Measured on one full evidence
set:

| | confluence | ml | score |
|---|---|---|---|
| OLD bullish | 0.8 | 0.95 | **85.75** |
| OLD bearish | 0.2 | 0.05 | **60.25** |
| NEW either side | 0.6 | 0.45 | **74.25** |

**3. Fused blob re-read as raw input.** `rank_many` sniffed dict keys, so a
blob carrying `label` matched the ML branch and one carrying `total` matched
the confluence branch — a fused row silently gained components it never had.
An unrecognized ML label is now `unavailable`, not a silent HOLD.

## Tier change is honest, not a lowered bar

Thresholds are untouched. `test_rank_one_fuses_and_degrades` moves HIGH → MED
because the same row scores 74.25 instead of 85.75 — its inputs were being
flattered. The expectation was updated to the corrected value with the symmetry
assertion added inline. No test was skipped, xfailed, or loosened.

## Tests red before, green after

```
5 failed, 3 passed   ->   8 passed   ->   10 passed
```

## Mutations — all four killed

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| MUT1 `_norm_conf` missing → 0.5 | 2 failed |
| MUT2 `_norm_ml` missing → 0.5 | 1 failed |
| MUT3 `_norm_ml` old asymmetric map | 1 failed |
| MUT4 blob guard removed | 1 failed |

**MUT4 initially survived.** The fused `components` dict carries no
scorer-shaped keys, so no key-only assertion could distinguish it. Two tests
were added to pin the fused-marker guard specifically, after which it is killed.

## Gates

```
tests/services tests/routes: 4546 passed, 33 skipped in 244.34s
ruff check: All checks passed!
```

## Not claimed as fixed

- The route still supplies `confluence=None, ml=None` at `flowseeker.py:2614`
  and `:2684` despite the four-scorer description. Separate decision needed:
  connect causal producers, or label those dimensions unavailable.
- H2 scanner cursor/budget, H4 persistence, H5-H7 untouched by this PR.

## Standing caveat

Conviction fusion is a deterministic sort over recorded evidence. It is **not**
a calibrated win probability, and no tier here implies one. No profitability or
predictive claim is made or supported by these tests.

Refs: `.planning/INTEGRATION_H0_H7.md`



---

## Slice 2 — one availability boundary across all scorers (`b51ee581`)

The three normalizers had drifted, so `*_status` could not be trusted. Three
distinct meanings were being reported through two labels:

| payload | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `_norm_flow({})` | 0.0 / `ok` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_flow({"conviction": None})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_conf({"total": None})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_ml({})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |
| `_norm_ml({"prediction": None})` | 0.0 / `invalid` | 0.0 / `missing` |

The confluence case is a real integration boundary, not hypothetical.
`services.agent.confluence.score` returns `{"total": None,
"direction": "insufficient_evidence"}` when it has no coverage. The producer
says "insufficient evidence"; the ranker relabelled that as "invalid" — i.e.
"this producer emitted garbage". Different operational responses, and an
unlabelled 0.0 is worse than either: indistinguishable from a measured zero.

Malformed payloads still report `invalid`; a real 0.0 still reports `ok` with a
0.0 component. "Measured and neutral" stays distinguishable from "never
measured" while both contribute nothing.

### Confirmed against live production data, not a fixture

Real call to `/api/heatseeker/node-confluence?ticker=SPY` (136 strikes
considered), feeding its actual `rows[0]["confluence"]` into `rank_one`:

```
producer total           : None
producer direction       : insufficient_evidence
ranker confluence_status : missing          <- was "invalid"
ranker component         : 0.0
conviction               : 0.0 LOW
```

### A correction I made to my own work

I initially "simplified" the empty-dict clauses in all three normalizers as
redundant. That was **wrong for confluence** — `conf.get("total", 0)` defaults
to 0, not None — and the suite caught it. Reverted, and the reason is now a
comment so the next reader does not repeat it. The `_norm_flow` clause *is*
genuinely redundant; MUT7 survived its removal, so it was deleted rather than
left as untested code.

### Mutations, slice 2

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| MUT5 `total=None` guard removed | 2 failed |
| MUT6 confluence empty-dict removed | 1 failed |
| MUT7 flow empty-dict clause restored | **survived** → clause is dead, deleted |
| MUT8 ml null-prediction guard removed | 1 failed |
| MUT9 ml empty-dict guard removed | 1 failed |

### Gates

```
local  tests/services tests/routes : 4555 passed, 33 skipped, 0 failed
CI 36414866514 (b3874cc9)           : backend 6511 passed / 0 failed
                                     frontend 918 passed, ruff pass
```

## H2 headline claim: refuted, no code changed

"Cursor advances by limit modulo the truncated length; repeated calls scan the
identical top batch" does not describe this code. `advance_cursor` rotates over
the full universe size:

those dimensions unavailable." I traced the chain; the answer is the second
branch, on evidence.

dimension only when its `inputs_status == "ok"`. `node_brief` populates only

```
flow_prints        -> 0 rows
```

PR now produces — is:


phantom score.

## H6 — the evidence export leaked snapshot scope verbatim (`6dbe0bf3`) — SECURITY

Investigating the Muse handoff surfaced a real leak. The packet's **facts** are
a strict allowlist and were safe. The **envelope** was not:

```python
"scope": scope,      # solstice_evidence.py — verbatim copy
```

Anything the snapshot carried in `scope` left the process byte-identical.
Verified by hash rather than by eye — my display pipeline was masking the value
as `***`, which briefly made this *look* already-redacted and nearly hid it:

```
input hash  : f46033ac88af
output hash : f46033ac88af
byte-identical: True
secret present in serialized packet: True
```

Now gated by `_EXPORTABLE_SCOPE_KEYS` — an **allowlist**, so a new
credential-bearing scope key fails CLOSED instead of needing a denylist entry.
Without it, redaction held only as long as nobody added a key.

The real production scope is preserved exactly:

```
input scope : ['basis','expiries','formulaVersion','metric','signConvention']
output scope: ['basis','expiries','formulaVersion','metric','signConvention']
ALL PRESERVED: True
```

**Latent hole, not a breach that occurred** — the live packet was already clean
because production scope carries nothing sensitive. Closed before anything puts a
DSN into a snapshot scope.

New `tests/solstice/test_evidence_packet_redaction.py` (28 tests) covers the H6
edge cases against the real builder: 22 credential-shaped key names,
allowlist-not-passthrough, injected text quarantined as `UNTRUSTED_USER_TEXT`,
missing wall absent rather than zero-valued, empty snapshot not claiming
eligibility, and schema versioning. **One of these failed against the old code** —
that failure is the finding.

### Muse status: NOT connected

No documented read-only integration has been established, no local bundle
inspected, and no fallback connection prepared. The packet is the supported
fallback and is what exists. The existing packet already carries
`schema_version`, `scope.metric/basis/signConvention/formulaVersion`,
`quality.setupEligible` + `reasonCodes`, and
`environment.inventory_basis = CONVENTIONAL_PROXY` — an honest label that the
service does not know real dealer inventory. Recording the limitation rather than
pretending it is connected.

fix(conviction-rank): stop scoring absent evidence as neutral confidence

A missing scorer input was normalized to 0.5 instead of 0.0, so a setup with
no evidence at all scored 17.5 and outranked real-but-weak evidence. The
existing `*_status` fields already reported "missing", so the component value
contradicted the status the module itself reported.

Reproduction at d905c9d2, before the fix:

    ALL-MISSING conviction: 17.5 tier: LOW
    components: {'flow': 0.0, 'opportunity': 0.0, 'confluence': 0.5, 'ml': 0.5}
    statuses:   all four 'missing'

That 17.5 is 0.2*0.5 + 0.15*0.5, entirely from the two scorers that had no data.

Two further defects, both reproduced rather than assumed:

1. Direction was leaking into quality. `_norm_ml` mapped DOWN->0.0 and
   UP->1.0 and then applied confidence around 0.5, so a BULLISH label at 0.8
   confidence became 0.95 while the exact bearish mirror became 0.05. The
   module's own docstring says it "never invents direction". Equal evidence now
   yields equal quality; side is carried by `direction`, not by the magnitude.

2. `rank_many` re-read an already-fused `conviction` blob as if it were raw
   scorer input. A blob carrying `label` matched the ML branch and one
   carrying `total` matched the confluence branch, so a fused row silently
   gained components it never had -- the double-counting the audit described.
   An unrecognized ML label is now unavailable rather than a silent HOLD.

Evidence -- the asymmetry, identical inputs, opposite side:

    OLD components: {'flow': 0.9, 'opportunity': 0.8, 'confluence': 0.8, 'ml': 0.95} score: 85.75
    NEW components: {'flow': 0.9, 'opportunity': 0.8, 'confluence': 0.6, 'ml': 0.45} score: 74.25
    BEAR mirror OLD: 60.25  NEW: 74.25

Tier thresholds are unchanged. The same row moves HIGH -> MED because its
inputs were being flattered, not because the bar moved. test_rank_one_fuses_and_degrades
is updated to the corrected value with the symmetry assertion added inline;
no test was skipped, xfailed, or loosened to accommodate the change.

keys and so no key-only assertion could distinguish it. Two further tests were

fix(conviction-rank): one availability boundary across all four scorers

The three normalizers had drifted apart, so `*_status` could not be trusted to
tell a consumer whether evidence was measured. Three distinct meanings were
being reported through two labels:

  _norm_flow       {}                     -> 0.0 / "ok"       (absent, claimed measured)
  _norm_flow       {"conviction": None}   -> 0.0 / "invalid"  (absent, claimed malformed)
  _norm_conf       {"total": None}        -> 0.0 / "invalid"  (absent, claimed malformed)
  _norm_ml         {}                     -> 0.0 / "invalid"
  _norm_ml         {"prediction": None}   -> 0.0 / "invalid"

The confluence case is a real integration boundary, not a hypothetical.

"direction": "insufficient_evidence"}` when it has no coverage -- verified by
calling it. The producer says "insufficient evidence" and the ranker was
relabelling that as "invalid", i.e. "this producer emitted garbage". Those
demand different operational responses, and an unlabelled 0.0 is worse than
either: it is indistinguishable from a measured zero.

Every payload that carries no reading now normalizes to (0.0, "missing").
Genuinely malformed data keeps "invalid", and a real reading of 0.0 keeps
"ok" with a 0.0 component -- so "measured and neutral" stays distinguishable
from "never measured" while both contribute nothing to the fusion.

The FACTS in the packet are a strict allowlist -- each constructed field by field
-- so those were safe. But the packet ENVELOPE was not:

    "scope": scope,          # solstice_evidence.py, verbatim copy

Anything the snapshot carried in `scope` left the process byte-identical.
Measured with a hash comparison rather than by eye:

    input hash  : f46033ac88af
    output hash : f46033ac88af
    byte-identical: True
    secret present in serialized packet: True

An allowlist now gates the exported scope. This is deliberately an allowlist
rather than a denylist: a new credential-bearing scope key now fails CLOSED (it
is simply not exported) instead of requiring someone to remember to add it to a
blocklist. Without this, redaction held only as long as nobody added a key.

The live packet was already clean in practice -- the production scope carries
only expiries/metric/basis/signConvention/formulaVersion -- so this is a latent
hole, not a breach that occurred. It is closed before anything puts a DSN into a
snapshot scope, which is exactly what the export is one refactor away from.

Verified the real scope shape survives untouched:

    input scope : ['basis','expiries','formulaVersion','metric','signConvention']
    output scope: ['basis','expiries','formulaVersion','metric','signConvention']
    ALL PRESERVED: True

Tests: new tests/solstice/test_evidence_packet_redaction.py, 28 tests, covering
the H6 edge cases against the real builder -- credential-shaped key names (22
parametrized), allowlist-not-passthrough, injected user text quarantined as
UNTRUSTED_USER_TEXT and never typed as a measurement, missing wall absent rather
than zero-valued, empty snapshot degrading without claiming eligibility, and
schema versioning. One of these FAILED against the old code and is the reason
this commit exists.
Mutations: MUT19 allowlist removed -> 1 failed.
Gates: tests/solstice + tests/agent 711 passed; ruff clean.

fix(universe-scan): a broken budget governor must fail CLOSED, not open

`scan_batch` caught any exception from `peek_available` and substituted
`float("inf")`. A missing or unhealthy budget governor therefore produced
MORE permissive behavior than a working one: the scan spent freely and recorded
nothing.

Reproduced with a governor that raises:

    BEFORE  scanned: 2   skipped: []
    AFTER   scanned: 0   skipped: [{'ticker':'SPY','reason':'BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE'},
                                   {'ticker':'QQQ','reason':'BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE'}]

Bounding spend is the governor's entire purpose. Losing sight of it is the worst
possible moment to stop enforcing it -- an outage in the thing meant to cap
spend silently removed the cap.

New reason `BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE`, deliberately distinct from the existing
`BUDGET_UNAFFORDABLE`. "We could not ask" and "the answer was no" are different
operational states and a caller must be able to tell them apart: the first is
an infrastructure problem worth alerting on, the second is normal backpressure.
Collapsing them would hide the outage inside ordinary throttling.

This narrows behavior only in the degraded case. A working budget, including
one that legitimately reports exhaustion, is unaffected -- that path still
yields BUDGET_UNAFFORDABLE and is asserted separately.

Tests: 2 added, 19 pass in the file. The first test installs a build_heatmap
that raises if called, so a regression fails loudly rather than silently
resuming the spend.
Mutations: MUT20 fail-closed guard removed -> 2 failed.
Gates: services+routes+solstice 4872 passed, 33 skipped, 0 failed; ruff clean.
docs(planning): record the fail-closed budget governor fix

fix(fetch-coordinator): an unreachable budget governor must fail CLOSED

Second instance of the same defect fixed in ed58eb7c, in a different file.

`BudgetExhausted` was handled correctly and returned a degraded response. But
any OTHER exception from `acquire()` -- a governor that is down, unreachable,
or simply throwing -- was logged and then execution CONTINUED into the fetch:

    except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning("Budget acquire failed for %s: %s", key, exc)
    logger.info("Initiating external fetch for %s", key)   # <-- still fetched

Reproduced with a governor that raises:

    BEFORE  fetched despite governor error? True   response: {'ok': True}
    AFTER   external fetch does not run; caller gets a degraded response

So an outage in the mechanism meant to cap external spend silently removed the
cap, and the failure was invisible to the caller because the response looked
successful.

Now returns `degraded_response("budget_unavailable", ...)`, a new value distinct
from the existing `budget_exhausted`. That distinction is the point: "the
governor said no" is ordinary backpressure, while "we could not reach the
governor" is an infrastructure fault that needs to surface. Collapsing them would
bury the outage inside routine throttling.

Note the original fix attempt at this behavior was subtly wrong and the new
test caught it: `BudgetExhausted.__init__` is `(retry_after, reason)`, so a
positional message argument collides with the keyword and raises TypeError
*inside* acquire. That TypeError is then caught by the new fail-closed handler
and mislabeled as `budget_unavailable`. Production code was never wrong here --
only the test was -- but the failure mode is worth recording, because a genuine
exhaustion signal can be turned into a misleading infrastructure error by a
single wrong constructor call anywhere upstream.

Tests: 2 added. The first installs a fetcher that raises if called, so a
regression fails loudly rather than quietly resuming the spend. The second pins
that the two degraded states stay distinguishable end to end.

fix(admin): the window check ignored DST, so it ran an hour early

`/api/databento/usage` computed the current Eastern time as

    now_et = datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(hours=5)   # rough ET

That is EST and does not track daylight saving. Measured right now:

    real ET (UTC-4) : 09:42
    admin.py (UTC-5): 08:42
    discrepancy     : 59 minutes

For roughly five months a year this endpoint reported the trading window CLOSED
a full hour before the trade route at `server._flow_stream` opened it. Two
endpoints disagreeing about whether it was 09:00, and anything gating on
`in_window_now` getting the wrong answer.

The trade route already did this correctly with `zoneinfo`. Rather than write a
third calculation, this now delegates to the existing authoritative helper
`server._in_window_now_et`. One source of truth for "is it open".

Chasing this also fixed a latent test bug. `test_flow_spy_outside_window_emits_error`
was failing in the full suite -- a pre-existing failure, confirmed identical on
base d905c9d2 in a clean worktree, not a regression from this branch. Its guard
`_in_window_now` returned False on ANY error, so "we could not tell" was treated
as "outside the window", and it asserted against a live stream during market
hours (where heartbeats are correct behavior). /api/databento/usage returns 503
without auth, so the key is absent entirely. The guard now returns None for
unknown and the test skips: an unobservable precondition is not a failed
precondition. That is the same fail-open-vs-fail-closed pattern already fixed in
universe_scan and fetch_coordinator this session.

currently open, so the outside-window assertion does not apply). New DST
regression test pins agreement with zoneinfo.

fix(friday-pin): the entry window ignored DST and fired an hour early

    # Convert to ET (UTC-5 or UTC-4 for DST)
    # Simple approximation: ET = UTC - 5h
    et_offset = timedelta(hours=5)
    ts_et = ts.astimezone(UTC) - et_offset

The comment said it handled DST. The code did not. This hardcodes EST, so for
roughly five months a year every bar was read an hour early.

The strategy gates on 15:30-15:40 ET. Measured on a real Friday in September:

    correct zoneinfo: Fri 15:35 EDT
    hardcoded -5h   : Fri 14:35
    15:35 inside 930-940 window? True
    14:35 inside 930-940 window? False

So during EDT the strategy evaluated bars an hour before its own entry window
and rejected the exact bars it exists to catch. Same seasonal bug as a134820e in
admin.py, found by sweeping for hardcoded ET offsets after that fix.

Now resolves the zone with `zoneinfo`, keeping the fixed offset only as a
fallback if the tz database is unavailable.

Note the mutation test mattered here. A first version of the test suite
re-implemented the window arithmetic in the test and asserted against that, and
the UTC-5 mutation SURVIVED it -- the tests were pinned to their own copy of the
logic, not to the production method. Rewritten to drive
`check_entry_condition` with a strategy primed to 40 flat bars (so the pin
condition always passes and only the clock can reject), which makes 15:35 ET
fire and 14:35 ET not fire. That kills the mutation: 3 failed.

tests/services/test_friday_pin_dst.py, 6 tests, previously no test file existed
for this strategy:
  - in-window Friday bar fires; out-of-window does not
  - boundaries 15:30/15:40 inclusive, 15:29/15:41 rejected
  - same ET time fires identically in EDT (Sep) and EST (Jan) -- the property a
    fixed offset cannot have
  - non-Friday still rejected
  - regression guard asserting UTC-5 would still miss the window
Mutations: MUT23 original UTC-5 restored -> 3 failed.
Gates: ruff clean.
docs(planning): record the DST sweep across admin and friday_pin

test(friday-pin): correct a fixture that encoded the same DST bug

The full suite caught 3 pre-existing friday_pin tests failing against the DST
fix in 68f3f216. Investigating rather than adjusting the fix:

    def make_friday_1535_et() -> datetime:
        """Create a Friday at 15:35 ET (20:35 UTC)."""
        dt = datetime(2026, 5, 22, 20, 35, tzinfo=UTC)  # Friday

2026-05-22 is in EDT, where 15:35 ET is 19:35 UTC -- not 20:35. The fixture
hardcoded the same UTC-5 offset as the production bug, so it asserted that a
15:35 bar should fire while actually delivering a 14:35 bar, and the two
errors cancelled. The test passed because it was wrong in the same direction as
the code.

This is the clearest example so far of why a green suite is not evidence: 15
friday_pin tests were green the whole time and none of them could have detected
the bug, because the fixture reproduced it.

The helper now builds the instant from the zone, so it is correct in either
season and the test asserts the real intent -- that a 15:35 ET bar fires.

Mutation now kills it much harder than the new DST file alone did:

    MUT23 (new DST tests only)   -> 3 failed
    MUT24 (both files)           -> 6 failed

The pre-existing tests now contribute three of those, which is the point: they
went from encoding the defect to detecting it.

24 passed. ruff clean.

test_signals_in_data hardcoded 20:35 UTC labelled "Friday 15:35 ET" -- the same

make_friday_1535_et() helper.

test_not_friday used 20:35 UTC on a Thursday. The weekday was still correct so
the test passed, but the instant was an hour off; now built from the zone so
the test varies only the weekday, not the time of day.

A negative test should isolate the one thing it is testing. This one also
changed the time, so a correct implementation could have rejected the bar for
the wrong reason.

rows.title: fix(truth-audit): match the subject line, not the whole commit message
rows.body:
Fixes the gate that blocked the #73 merge.

## The failure

The #73 merge commit (`433d99ab`) failed CI:

```
FAIL: Refactor commit: server.py must not grow (currently 4047 lines, baseline 3532)
```

The trigger was the word `refactor` appearing **once in the commit body**, in a
sentence explaining why the evidence-packet leak mattered. `server.py` was
already 4047 lines from earlier work that this commit never touched:

```
git diff --name-only 29f74d8a..a65f6a3a | grep -c server.py   -> 0
git show d905c9d2:backend/server.py | wc -l                    -> 4047
git show 29f74d8a:backend/server.py | wc -l                    -> 4047
```

A correct merge was blocked by a word in a sentence. `server.py` is frozen for
the integration lane, so the fix belongs in the gate, not the file.

## Root cause

Rules 1 and 2 gate on what a commit **claims to do**, so they must read the
subject line. They matched the entire message instead, making a commit
*describing* work indistinguishable from one *declaring* it.

The script already knew this. Its own comments record that Rules 9-12 hit the
identical problem and were scoped to the subject — *"this very rule blocked its
own commit that way on the first try."* Rules 1 and 2 were never brought in
line. `COMMIT_SUBJECT` is now defined once, above Rule 1; the duplicate
definition further down is removed.

## The rule is not neutered

Verified in both directions:

- Current tree: **227 passed, 0 failed**
- A synthetic commit whose **subject** is `refactor: reorganize backend` still
  fails Rule 2 (**226 passed, 1 failed**)

A real refactor claim is still caught, which is the point of the rule.

Also: the `Message:` banner previously echoed `git log` while the rules read a
separately-derived first line, so the audit could print something it had not
actually evaluated. One variable now feeds both.

rows.title: fix(alerts): a boolean was broadcast as a bearish momentum alert
rows.body:
A boolean could be broadcast to every `/ws/signals` client as a bearish
momentum alert.

## The bug

`_parse_momentum_score` coerced with `int(float(raw))`. Since `bool` subclasses
`int`, `float(True)` is `1.0` — so a boolean became a real score of **1**:

```
MOMENTUM_EXTREME_HIGH = 80      # score > 80 -> extreme bullish
MOMENTUM_EXTREME_LOW  = 20      # score < 20 -> extreme bearish
```

Measured before the fix:

| input | parsed | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `True` | 1 | **BEARISH ALERT** |
| `False` | 0 | **BEARISH ALERT** |
| `85` | 85 | BULLISH ALERT |
| `10` | 10 | BEARISH ALERT |

This is the live signal path: the resulting alert goes to `broadcast_signal`
and reaches every connected `/ws/signals` client, so a value that was never a
measurement could appear in the UI as *"Strong BEARISH momentum — score 1/100"*.

Booleans are now rejected like any other malformed input.

## The 50 fallback, and why it stays

It is a **no-alert sentinel, not a measurement** — 50 sits inside the dead band
(20..80), so unavailable momentum cannot fire an alert. That was luck rather
than design, so it is now asserted: if the thresholds move, absent data starts
broadcasting alerts and these tests fail.

A real reading of 50 and unavailable data still return the same value.
Distinguishing them properly means returning a status alongside the score, which
is a wider change to the detector contract than this fix should make on its own.

## Tests

2 added to `tests/routes/test_alert_plumbing.py`. One failed against the old
code with `bool True must not become a score, got 1`.

- `test_booleans_are_not_momentum_scores`
- `test_missing_and_malformed_are_not_measured_neutral_readings`

MUT26 (bool guard removed) → 1 failed.

## Sibling sweep

The other 13 broad-`except` sites in `routes/` were checked for the same shape.
They are correct — each leaves the key **absent** rather than fabricating a
value, with the degradation documented inline (`steal_three.py:224`,
`ml_api.py:554` paper metrics; `analytics.py:372` cache). `alerts.py:59` was
already correct for the same reason.

## Gates

`tests/routes` 346 passed; ruff clean.

rows.title: fix(observability): the health endpoint 500'd during exactly the outages it exists to report
rows.body:
Three fixes, all found by verifying behavior rather than trusting green tests.

## 1. The health endpoint 500'd during exactly the outages it exists to report

Found by probing the running server — the test suite was green throughout.

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' localhost:8000/api/data/health
500
```

`ProviderStats.seconds_since_last_success` returned `float("inf")` when a
provider had never succeeded. That propagated into the `provider_down` alert
dict, and `inf` is not JSON compliant, so response encoding raised
`ValueError`.

The route's own `except Exception` could not catch it — **serialization happens
after the handler returns, outside the try block.** So a provider that had never
succeeded took the health endpoint down with it. The 200 was only reachable
because no provider had been recorded yet.

Fixed to `None`. Alerting semantics preserved deliberately: a never-succeeded
provider is a *stronger* statement than "more than N seconds ago", so it still
fires `provider_down`:

```python
is_down = since is None or since > self.provider_down_seconds
```

The Prometheus gauge cannot hold `None`, and `0` would read as "just
succeeded" — the opposite of the truth — so the gauge uses `+inf`, which a
Gauge *can* hold.

Same class in the vol models: `rmse = inf` across 9 sites in
`SABRModel.fit` / `SVIProfile.fit`. Reachable through the
`POST /api/vol-surface/{t}/sabr` guard, since negative/NaN vols are filtered
*internally* after the `len >= 4` check. Behind auth, so latent rather than
live — I verified that before spending time on it.

## 2. A test making 75 real calls to api.public.com

`test_total_provider_failure_is_unavailable_then_stale` called `get_movers()`
**unconditionally**, and guarded only its *assertions*:

```python
stale = asyncio.run(movers_svc.get_movers(limit=5))   # always ran
live = movers_svc.completed_session_pair(now=datetime.now(UTC))
if live == (last, prior):                             # only this was guarded
```

`get_movers` fans out over the full 75-ticker universe. On any day the pair
differed, the test still made 75 outbound requests and discarded the response.

Caught by the session-scoped guard in `tests/offline_network.py`, which
correctly fails closed — but it asserts at *teardown*, so the failure surfaced
against whichever test ran last and pointed at the wrong file entirely. That's
why it appeared as an unrelated error in `test_wall_restore_latest.py`.

```
before: 651 passed, 1 error in 18.40s
after:  651 passed, 0 error in  8.85s
```

The ~10s drop is the 75 blocked network attempts no longer made.

## 3. `_reset_state` left the shared budget poisoned

`test_upstream_seam_calls_real_adapter_signature_and_shape` failed in CI with
`Expected mock to have been awaited once. Awaited 0 times`, and passed in
isolation — which is what made it look order-random.

`public_budget.budget` is a module-level singleton whose state outlives a
test. `market_bars._reset_state()` cleared the bar cache, quarantine counter
and last-error field, but **not the budget**. With a cooldown still active,
`_get` returned early at the budget gate and never reached the broker.

```
before: RESULT bars: None       RESULT awaited: 0
after:  RESULT bars: [...1 bar] RESULT awaited: 1
```

Draining tokens was not enough — the budget refills. It is specifically the
cooldown that reproduces this.

## Tests

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| `tests/routes` + `tests/solstice` | 651 passed |
| `tests/services` + `test_r7_1_red` | 4245 passed, 33 skipped |
| `tests/services/test_market_bars_reset_state.py` | 3 passed |
| `tests/test_movers_route.py` | 2 passed |

Mutations, all killed: MUT27 `seconds_since_last_success` → inf (5 failed),
MUT28 `is_down` ignores None (2 failed), MUT29 rmse → inf (2 failed),
MUT30 budget reset removed (3 failed).

The new budget tests drive the real seam through a mocked broker, so they
exercise the actual budget gate rather than asserting on the reset helper.

docs(planning): record the #79 bool-coercion alert fix

Item 2c. The signal-path sweep that found the momentum bool bug and the
13 sibling broad-except sites that were already correct.

fix(observability): the health endpoint 500'd during exactly the outages it exists to report

`GET /api/data/health` returned HTTP 500. Found by probing the running server,
not the test suite -- the suite was green throughout.

    $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' localhost:8000/api/data/health
    500

Cause: `ProviderStats.seconds_since_last_success` returned `float("inf")` when
a provider had never succeeded. That value propagated into the `provider_down`
alert dict, and `inf` is not JSON compliant, so response encoding raised
`ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: inf`.

The route's own `except Exception` could not catch it. Serialization happens
AFTER the handler returns, outside the try block. So a provider that had never
succeeded took the health endpoint down with it -- it went dark precisely when
a provider was down and there was something to report. The 200 was only
reachable because no provider had been recorded yet.

Reproduced deterministically in-process, matching the live response exactly:

    RESULT 500 {"error":"Internal server error","type":"ValueError",...}

`None` is both serializable and more honest: "no success has happened yet" is
an absent measurement, not an infinitely long one. After:

    RESULT 200 {"providers":{"databento":{...,"seconds_since_last_success":null,...}}}

Alerting semantics are preserved deliberately. A never-succeeded provider is a
stronger statement than "more than N seconds ago", so it still fires
provider_down -- `is_down = since is None or since > threshold`. Only
`window_calls > 0` gates it, i.e. we have actually tried to reach the provider.

The Prometheus gauge cannot hold None, and 0 would read as "just succeeded" --
the opposite of the truth -- so the gauge uses +inf, which a Gauge CAN hold, to
distinguish "never succeeded" from "succeeded moments ago". The alert dict
carries the honest None.

SABRModel.fit and SVIProfile.fit used `rmse = inf` as their "no fit achieved"
sentinel across 9 sites. Reachable through the guard: POST
/api/vol-surface/{ticker}/sabr checks `len >= 4`, but negative/NaN vols are
filtered *internally* afterwards, so four strikes can reduce to too few and
return `rmse: inf` -> 500. Now None plus an explicit fit_status.

fix(eastern-clock): US DST rule for all four ET gates, rebased on #84

The host-tm_isdst fallback existed in four places, each gating something
that matters:

  server._in_window_now_et      the 09:00-10:30 ET live window
  server._scheduler_loop        OI prefetch gate
  server.flow_sse               the trading-window gate on real streaming
  alert_dispatcher._is_quiet_hours   whether an outbound call is suppressed

`time.localtime().tm_isdst` reports the HOST timezone, not Eastern's. US and
EU DST begin and end on different dates, so for roughly Mar 8-28 and Oct 25-31
each year the host's answer is wrong about Eastern's. A one-hour error opens
or closes a window at the wrong time, and on the quiet-hours gate it lands
directly on the 22:00/21:59 boundary.

The arithmetic now lives in services/eastern_clock.py and applies the US rule
directly (second Sunday in March 07:00 UTC -> first Sunday in November
06:00 UTC), needing no tz database and correct wherever the host runs.
`grep tm_isdst` over production code returns one hit: a docstring saying why.

_in_window_now_et now fails closed if even the arithmetic fallback raises.

19 tests across three files, each driving the real function with zoneinfo
forced to fail and time.localtime reporting a foreign host's DST flag.
MUT30/31/32 all killed.
